newsitem.title: UK: Ldn gold conquered by bears, fixed at 11-week low.
newsitem.headline: Ldn gold conquered by bears, fixed at 11-week low.

text.p: Gold fixed at $338.95 an ounce on Tuesday, the lowest level since February 12, as increasing prospects of future IMF gold sales dealt a fresh blow to the weakening metal.
Negative sentiment crept across the precious metals complex after a sell-off on Monday following the expiry of options contracts which also led to a breakdown in silver.

"There must be a gravitational pull to towards the year low ($336.90) and as that's a four-year low, it opens up a lot of chart territory," said precious metals analyst Andy Smith at Union Bank of Switzerland.
By 1030 GMT spot gold was indicated at $338.90 versus New York's close of $339.45/$339.95. Silver edged two cents lower to $4.63/$4.65, while platinum shed 50 cents to $372.50/$373.50.
"It's difficult to see what's going to take gold higher other than short covering," commented one gold dealer.
Smith noted that according to data from New York's Comex gold futures exchange, the large U.S. investment funds were positioning themselves in expectation of lower gold prices.
"That seems entirely logical given that we have had a rise in U.S. interest rates, a strengthening dollar and an orderly correction on Wall Street," he said.

Sentiment turned negativite on the announcement that the hitherto staunchly pro-gold Swiss government would hold a referendum on reducing the gold backing of the Swiss franc, to revalue its gold reserves and sell part of its surplus gold.
On Tuesday the Swiss were also backing IMF gold sales if money from rich nations was not enough to cut third world debt.

Gold bears also played on a report that the German Bundesbank could look at revaluing gold reserves after it repeatedly denied market talk that this was considered an option for entry into a European single currency.
Technical price charts were also gloomy, signalling a drop to $325, the lowest level since March 1993, if $336.15 faltered.
"While it's below $345, $336.15 looks very much under pressure," said Karen Jones, a chart analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston. "If that doesn't hold there is not a lot between there and $325.10."
But traders said cheaper gold could tempt physical buyers and shorts to cover their positions against a possible delivery.
"Probably most people are trading this from the short side. That could be the saviour of the market," said a dealer.
Silver's prospects were also battered after it breached important support of $4.70 on Monday and hit a two-year low of $4.59. A slide to 4.33 was now on the cards, analysts said.
Palladium bucked the trend as it gained 50 cents on Tuesday to $157.25/$158.28 as fears over further delays in Russian supplies continued.
